t: This is the statue of Peter Pan, which stands in Kensington Gardens to the west of the Long Water, close to J. M. Barrie's former home on Bayswater Road. Barrie commissioned it, and Sir George Frampton made it in 1912. It stands at the spot where, in Barrie's 1902 book The Little White Bird, Peter Pan lands after flying out of his nursery. Frampton made six other casts, which now stand in other places around the world.
